question: Which elections are unwinnable? (hidden-world features → loss)

x10_duplication.match_rule: same seed/manifesto/policy, |ΔE| <= 1e-5 (GPU float atomics) and the same victory

definitions.oracle_loss: ORACLE (oracle manifesto + ORACLE planner) lost at ₫500 (X0 for seeds 100xx, X6 for 120xx)
definitions.oracle_margin / bayes_margin: expected share E − 0.5 of that game
definitions.start_share: true E after the ORACLE manifesto commit, before round 1 (no campaign)
definitions.tv_two_largest: total-variation distance between the archetype means of the two largest regions
definitions.tv_mean_pair: mean pairwise archetype TV over the 4 regions
definitions.p_g_mean: mean realised SBM inter-region probability p_rs (off-diagonal), the network's fragmentation (low = fragmented)
definitions.p_g_two_largest: p_rs between the two largest regions
definitions.lambda2_L: algebraic connectivity λ₂ of the Laplacian
definitions.largest_P1..P3: personality of the largest region (P0 = reference)
definitions.models: standardised features; (a) ridge-logistic (λ=1, intercept free) with 2000 stratified bootstrap CIs; ridge-linear for margins; (b) depth-3 CART (Gini / MSE, min leaf 5)
definitions.cv: 5-fold stratified CV repeated 20× (standardisation inside folds): AUC (class) or R² (reg); permutation null with 200 label shuffles (2 repeats each)
definitions.top3: the three features with the largest |standardised logistic/linear coefficient|

bayes_loss.reason: only 2 events: too few for a regression, a tree or a 5-fold CV AUC

hypotheses.family: H1–H3, one-sided Mann–Whitney (H1, H2), chi-square (H3); Holm

tests.name: H1 tv_two_largest higher in ORACLE-loss worlds
H2 p_g_mean lower in ORACLE-loss worlds
H3 largest-region personality ~ best paid channel (chi-square, X0 ₫500)

channel_by_personality.source: X0 ₫500, informed manifesto + pay_workers / pay_media / pay_split

classes.close_call: lost within 0.01 of 50% in E: the election draw decided
classes.divided_majority: the two largest regions want different things (archetype TV distance in the top tercile) and the manifesto starts low (start share in the bottom tercile)
classes.low_start: the best manifesto starts low (start share in the bottom tercile)
classes.divided_regions: two largest regions far apart (TV in the top tercile)
classes.fragmented_network: few links between regions (p_g in the bottom tercile)
classes.independent_largest: the largest region is P2 Independent (low susceptibility to every channel)

deviations: X10's default cell (N=1e4, T=5, ₫500, seeds 10000–10049) re-runs the X0 ₫500 worlds: 550/550 rows agree within 1e-5 in E with the same result (max |ΔE| 3.0e-07, GPU float atomics), so it adds no new world; counted once.
Bayes loss has only 2 events in 100 X6 worlds: no regression, tree or CV AUC is fitted for it. The two losses are listed, and the Bayes margin E − 0.5 (continuous) is modelled instead.
ORACLE loss at ₫500 has 11 events in 200 worlds; the logistic model uses a weak ridge (λ=1) and every CV AUC comes with a permutation null.
Supplementary targets not in the plan: People Pleaser loss (27 events), start share and the margins.
scikit-learn is not installed in the env: logistic, ridge, CART, AUC and partial dependence are numpy implementations in this script.
CPU only (plan §1.1 point 5 lists the X15 fitting as a CPU exception); features use the SciPy spectra (N = 1e4 < GPU_SPECTRA_MIN_N).

provenance.parity: not applicable (no simulation; CPU fitting is a §1.1 exception)
